hits.label: What Connect actually depends on
hits.text: what connect actually depends on you cannot debug a contact center if you treat aws as a logo on the invoice. amazon connect, called amazon connect customer in the admin guide after the 28 april 2026 family announcement, is a multi-tenant contact center in a region you choose. the instance does not contain iam, s3, lambda, kinesis, or cloudwatch. it calls them. this campus starts here because every later fault lands in one of those services: a key policy, a log group, a stream shard, a regional endpoint, or a firewall. the family name amazon connect now covers customer, health, decisions, and talent. this campus teaches the contact center. iam prefixes you will meet include connect, profile, cases, wisdom, and voiceid. voiceid is historical after 20 may 2026. the data plane for agents is the browser, not a pbx firmware image. shared responsibility: aws runs the platform. you run flows, identity, keys, numbers, quotas, and the agent network. starting in the flow designer before you can name the region and the account.

hits.label: Regions, endpoints, and why Osaka is special
hits.text: regions, endpoints, and why osaka is special a region is a capacity, latency, and residency boundary. it is not a checkbox you can flip on a live number. the instance, its numbers, and its logs are regional. global resiliency is the only supported way to link two instances, and only in published pairs: northern virginia with oregon, frankfurt with london, tokyo with osaka. osaka is a replica region for tokyo. numbers have to be enabled for global resiliency, and delivery through osaka can take up to 20 seconds. that is a design input, not a footnote. new accounts start at two instances per region. quota raises are per region. raising oregon does not raise virginia. the ccp domain is instance.my.connect.aws. the old awsapps.com domain is documented as going away. softphone turn endpoints are regional. a laptop in another country still talks to the instance region. putting the 'second region' in a city that is not in a supported pair and calling it resiliency.

hits.label: IAM is not the security profile
hits.text: iam is not the security profile agents get a security profile. automations get an iam principal. mixing the names produces a policy that cannot place a call and a user who can. a security profile decides which buttons a user sees in the admin site and the ccp. an iam policy decides which aws api calls a role may make. connect also relies on resource policies, especially lambda:invokefunction for principal connect.amazonaws.com. the service-linked role is what connect uses to write recordings and logs. a customer-managed kms key still needs a key policy that trusts that role, or the put succeeds in your mind and fails in s3. connect:startoutboundvoicecontact and startchatcontact are privileged. do not put them on a public web role. profile and cases are separate iam services. wisdom is still the prefix you will see for agent assist in the service authorization reference. least privilege means the instance arn, not resource star, once the design is real. granting an agent administratoraccess because the security profile looked empty.

hits.label: Kinesis is how the ecosystem listens
hits.text: kinesis is how the ecosystem listens anything that must react to agents or to finished contacts needs a stream, not a person refreshing a report. agent events and contact trace records can go to kinesis data streams or firehose. streams let several consumers read. firehose is the buffered path to s3. one quiet five-minute stretch is the documented moment to look at delivery errors. a single shard is a common starting size for agent events and a common cause of lag once wfm and a custom dashboard both read it. ctrs are near real time, not instant, and consumers must tolerate duplicates. only one firehose is the default ctr delivery. fan out by consuming a stream. join on contactid. there is no other honest key. agent events are the adherence feed. historical reports are not. pointing two wfm products at one shard and discovering lag during a monday peak.

hits.label: The network path is part of the product
hits.text: the network path is part of the product connect's softphone is webrtc in the agent's browser. a firewall designed for a desk phone will block it. option 1 is a domain allow list: the instance on tcp 443, telemetry, transport, and turnnlb on udp 3478. option 2 is the aws ip ranges and is documented as not recommended. test more than 200 calls. an error rate above 2 percent points at proxy or dns resolution. media should not hairpin through a vpn. stateless firewalls also need the browser's ephemeral udp range, because there is no lasting 'pin' the way people imagine. the usual failure string names turn:turnnlb and port 3478. ice_collection_timeout means the browser never gathered candidates. a custom ccp can be media-less, but then you still do not have a softphone. video adds a chime subnet and does not support vdi. opening tcp 443 and declaring the softphone done.

hits.label: Certifications and the badges that are not certifications
hits.text: certifications and the badges that are not certifications there is no amazon connect specialty exam on the aws certification catalog. pretending a badge is that exam misleads a hiring plan. the catalog's foundational exams are aws certified cloud practitioner and aws certified ai practitioner. the associate exam that best covers the surrounding design is aws certified solutions architect - associate. developer - associate fits lambda and streams. cloudops engineer - associate fits quotas and operations. security - specialty fits iam and kms. aws certified advanced networking - specialty is the exam for complex networks, and its last day is 31 december 2026. connect-specific recognition is a set of skill builder learning plans with credly badges, passed at 80 percent: communications specialist, fundamentals, ai fundamentals, and developer, plus an administrator track. cloud practitioner is the shared vocabulary of accounts, regions, and billing. ai practitioner is context for generative features. it does not configure a flow. the communications specialist badge covers telephony, ivr, flows, routing, and omnichannel. a badge is issued through credly within about two weeks of the knowledge check. it is not a proctored certification. listing 'connect certified' on a design document because someone finished a free knowledge check.

hits.label: A depends-on map you can defend
hits.text: a depends-on map you can defend every later track names the foundation it needs. if that foundation is missing, the track's lab will show the same fault. telephony depends on the instance and on quotas. flows depend on telephony only because a number has to enter somewhere. lambda depends on iam. the ccp depends on the network lesson. analytics depends on kinesis and s3. global resiliency depends on identity, numbers, and a supported region pair. the ecosystem track depends on all of those, because wfm, quality, e911, and the crm are consumers of contactid, recordings, agent events, and profiles. read the depends-on line on each track before you skip ahead. a migration bridge without flows and routing is a glossary, not a plan. e911 depends on profiles, lambda, and an outbound whisper flow. price estimates depend on the rate card date, which this campus stamps as 14 october 2026. treating tracks as independent products.

hits.text: feature timeline names moved. features mostly stayed. voice id did not. the timeline in this campus is a study map. dates come from aws what's new, the admin guide, the aws news blog, or a compiled timeline that cites those pages and was checked on 25 september 2026. where the admin guide applies the 2026 product name to a 2017 row, the timeline keeps the name used on the day. read it before you use an old runbook. contact lens means conversational analytics. amazon q in connect means agent assist. high-volume outbound means campaigns. voice id means ended. 2017-03-28, launch. 2020-07-23, contact lens generally available. 2026-04-28, the family announcement. 2026-05-20, voice id end of support. quoting a document-history row's 2026 wording as if that was the 2017 name.

hits.label: Create the instance on purpose
hits.text: create the instance on purpose the instance is the tenancy boundary for users, flows, and numbers. an accidental second instance splits reports and identity. you choose identity at creation: connect-stored users or saml 2.0. you choose whether the instance places and receives calls, and where recordings and reports go. changing identity later is a project, not a toggle. the admin url and the ccp live on the instance alias under my.connect.aws. write the alias down. firewalls and saml acs urls depend on it. default concurrent calls: 10. request more before a pilot that is larger than a team. storage choices can be updated, but existing objects do not move themselves. two instances per region is the starting quota. cloudtrail records the control-plane calls. turn it on in the account, not inside the flow. creating a production instance in the wrong region because the console opened there.

hits.label: SAML attributes that make a user real
hits.text: saml attributes that make a user real a successful saml login that lands without a routing profile is a user who cannot take a contact. map the role, the security profile, and the routing profile from the assertion. hierarchy is optional and easy to get wrong if your idp sends a display name and connect expects the configured group. iam identity center is a reasonable idp. it still federates with saml. global resiliency adds a regional sign-in endpoint. the ccp allow list includes it only when you have onboarded. test with one user and one profile before you federate the whole center. role session name problems show up as opaque access errors. read the idp logs and the connect login error together. do not create a parallel local admin and forget it when people leave. the replica instance needs the same identity story or failover signs nobody in. declaring saml done because the idp returned a success code.

hits.label: CloudFormation, CDK, and Terraform
hits.text: cloudformation, cdk, and terraform clicking the console does not review. a stack does. the resource types you will actually diff are aws::connect::instance, contactflow, contactflowmodule, hoursofoperation, queue, routingprofile, user, securityprofile, phonenumber, quickconnect, rule, and trafficdistributiongroup. flow content is flow-language json. terraform mirrors the important ones, including aws_connect_lambda_function_association and aws_connect_bot_association. association resources are how code attaches lambda and lex. the flow still has to reference them. cdk uses the same cloudformation types. phone number resources can fail for quota reasons the template cannot see. do not put production flow json only in a laptop. the json is the source of truth the designer also edits, so pick one writer. aws-samples and amazon-connect/amazon-connect-streams are the public code to read, not to paste into production unchanged. exporting a flow once and calling the export a pipeline.

hits.label: Prompts, statuses, and the small quotas
hits.text: prompts, statuses, and the small quotas the limits that surprise people are the ones marked not adjustable. you get 500 prompts, 50 agent statuses, and 100 security profiles to start. status count cannot be raised. a status per team, per language, and per campaign will hit 50. prompts stored in s3 are called out as not fully replicated by global resiliency the way built-in prompts are. say that in the failover test. name prompts for the flow that uses them. custom statuses feed wfm only if the wfm mapping knows the name. reports: 2000 per instance, and every saved personal report counts. user hierarchy groups: 500 across all levels. creating a status called lunch-team-a through lunch-team-z.

hits.label: DID, toll-free, shared cost, UIFN
hits.text: did, toll-free, shared cost, uifn the number type is a cost and a failure-domain choice. connect sells four types, in more than 100 countries, billed per day plus per-minute telephony. a us did in the oregon worked example is 0.030 usd per day, 0.0022 usd per inbound minute, and outbound us telephony at 0.0048 usd per minute. us toll-free numbers are registered with somos. aws can place them on more than one carrier, which is why they cost more and why they are the more resilient public number. the appendix example charges 0 usd per day for the first 12 months of the free tier and 0.06 usd per day after. country rates that are not in that example must be read from the global telephony table, not invented. did is one carrier. it presents a local number. it is not load-balanced across carriers. you can mix did and toll-free on one instance. inbound telephony in the example is charged per minute with a 60 second minimum. voice service is a second charge, 0.038 or 0.018 usd per minute depending on the product form, billed per second with a 10 second minimum. quoting a toll-free per-minute rate you did not look up.

hits.label: Claiming and the false 'limit' on the first number
hits.text: claiming and the false 'limit' on the first number the first claim is a support conversation more often than people expect. the default quota is 10 numbers per instance, and it is adjustable. the docs also say you can see 'you've reached the limit of phone numbers' the first time you claim, and that those failures need support. concurrent campaign calls default to 0. outbound calling destinations are allowed by country. a new instance that cannot dial the country you care about is a quota or a country allow list, not a flow bug. raise the call concurrency quota before you publish the number. associate the number with a flow or the caller hears nothing useful. for global resiliency, numbers join a traffic distribution group. write down the carrier and the country. porting later depends on both. retrying the claim button until it works.

hits.label: Porting without losing the rollback
hits.text: porting without losing the rollback a port is a date with the losing carrier. it is not a flow change. you submit the port with the same kind of support request the quota page describes. you need a letter of authorization and a firm order commit date. until that date, the old platform still owns the number. dual-run means the old platform and connect are both built, and you can move the number back if the first day fails. practice the rollback before the port window, not during it. match the caller id and any cnam story you actually have. do not promise caller-name display the product does not set. internal extensions can stay on cucm. only the public number has to move. update the crm screen pop to the new contactid in the same window. tell the wfm and recording tools the storage path before the port, or the first day has no recordings in the old tool. porting on friday because the flow 'looks done'.

hits.label: SIP, external voice, and what is not a trunk in the CUCM sense
hits.text: sip, external voice, and what is not a trunk in the cucm sense connect does not give you a cucm sip trunk page. it gives you native telephony, transfers to numbers, and an external voice connector for analytics. transfer to phone number is how a flow or an agent sends a call to a cucm route point, a webex calling number, or a mobile. the call leaves connect and the other system owns the media from there. the pricing appendix describes an external voice connector at 0.032 usd per minute and 100 usd per connector per day, for analytics on voice that stays on another system. the default quota for external voice analytics connectors is 0 until you request them. that is a different product from claiming a did. do not design a sip trunk in cucm and assume connect will register to it as a phone. one-way audio after a transfer is often the other system's codec or network, not the ccp. external voice is for analytics on audio you already have. campaign answering-machine detection is check call progress, and only in campaign flows. drawing a sip trunk icon between cucm and connect and assigning a dial-peer as if both were cucm.

hits.label: Outbound calls and caller ID
hits.text: outbound calls and caller id outbound is a queue setting, a permission, and a country quota. the queue's outbound caller id is the number the customer sees. it must be a number you are allowed to present. the origination number on a 911 call is the same idea: responders can call back only if that number accepts inbound calls. high-volume outbound became outbound campaigns on 20 june 2022. campaign voice on connect customer is 0.045 usd per minute instead of 0.038. startoutboundvoicecontact is an api. guard it. an outbound whisper flow runs before the customer and agent join. recording for outbound is set there. call phone number is the block that dials from an outbound whisper flow. country allow lists block destinations even when the flow is correct. using a personal mobile as the outbound caller id.

hits.label: Flow types are not one canvas
hits.text: flow types are not one canvas each flow type only offers the blocks that make sense there. a hold flow is not a place to transfer to a queue and hope. inbound flows greet and route. customer queue flows run while the customer waits and can offer a callback. hold flows loop prompts. whisper flows play just before the join. transfer-to-agent and transfer-to-queue flows are what quick connects run. disconnect flows run after the end. outbound whisper flows are where you set outbound recording and where call phone number belongs. a customer queue flow is interruptible. transfer to queue inside a customer queue flow moves a contact that is already queued. end flow / resume ends the flow and does not hang up. disconnect hangs up. putting the hold music in the inbound flow and wondering why hold is silent.

hits.label: The block catalog, grouped by job
hits.text: the block catalog, grouped by job you do not memorize fifty icons. you group them by the job they do. control blocks move the contact: play prompt, get customer input, distribute by percentage, loop, wait, transfer to flow, end flow, disconnect. data blocks read and write attributes, metrics, profiles, cases, and data tables. routing blocks set the queue, the criteria, the priority, and then transfer. integration blocks call lambda, lex through get customer input, a module, an external tool, or an ai agents domain. the full list in the designer is the source of truth. this campus includes every block from that list in the lab palette and the glossary. check hours, check queue status, check staffing, and get metrics are how a flow refuses work it cannot staff. set logging and set recording are how you can prove what happened. show view is the step-by-step guide. agentic cx and connect assistant are the 2026 ai entry points. voice id blocks remain on the list and should not be added. support ended 20 may 2026. using a block because it is visible, including voice id.

hits.label: Attributes are the only memory the next system gets
hits.text: attributes are the only memory the next system gets if it is not an attribute, the crm, the whisper, and the ctr cannot see it. set contact attributes writes strings. check contact attributes branches on them. lambda and lex write them too. names are case-sensitive in practice. pick a prefix for your company and do not collide with system attributes. the screen pop, the case field, and the wfm code all want the same customer id. write it once, early, before any transfer. system attributes include the queue, the channel, and the customer endpoint. lex exposes intent and slots. copy the ones you care about into your own names. a transfer to another flow keeps the contact attributes. a transfer to a phone number leaves connect. attributes do not ride the pstn. asking the customer for an account number and never storing it.

hits.label: Modules are how you stop copying flows
hits.text: modules are how you stop copying flows a copied inbound flow drifts. a module has one published body. invoke module runs a published module. return (from module) ends it successfully. the default quota is 200 modules. inputs and outputs should be attributes you have named, not a comment in the designer. global resiliency replicates modules. a module that calls a lambda in only one region will fail in the other region unless the function is there too. publish, then invoke. a draft module is not what production runs. keep authentication, language selection, and recording policy in modules. version the module in your stack as contactflowmodule json. test the module with the same error branches as a flow. fixing a bug in one of eight copied flows.

hits.label: Every error branch is a product decision
hits.text: every error branch is a product decision an unconnected error output hangs up. that is a choice, even if you did not mean it. lambda has success, error, and, when synchronous, timeout. lex and get customer input have error and timeout paths. hours have in and out. transfers have capacity and error paths. connect each one to a prompt a human would accept. distribute by percentage is for a measured pilot. it is not a skills router. loop can spin. cap it. turn logging on before the first test call. the disconnect flow does not save you from an error hang-up. the customer is already gone. wait and play prompt are how you avoid silence during async lambda. touchtone buffer lets callers type ahead. turn it on only if the prompts allow it. leaving the red error port empty because the happy path worked once.

hits.label: The flow language is how instances share a design
hits.text: the flow language is how instances share a design the designer is a view. the json is what you review and promote. an action has a type, parameters, and transitions. conditions can nest no more than five deep, with no more than 50 sub-conditions. operators compare strings and numbers. a non-numeric comparison against greaterthan returns false. action kinds are contact, participant, interaction, and flow control. participant actions such as play prompt need a participant. some disconnect flows do not have one. use the json to move a flow between a test instance and production. do not hand-edit a 2,000-line export without a diff. modules have their own json. the api still says amazon connect in places. the admin guide may say connect customer. the json types are what the api accepts. treating a screenshot of the designer as the source of truth.

hits.label: Get customer input is the Lex block
hits.text: get customer input is the lex block there is no separate 'lex block' to hunt for. get customer input is where the bot is selected. you associate a lex v2 bot alias with the instance, often with aws_connect_bot_association or the console, and then the block chooses that alias. the default quota is 70 bots and 100 v2 aliases. on connect customer the worked pricing example charges 0 usd for the lex speech requests themselves. you still pay for the voice minutes. branch on the intent name you configured, not on the sentence the caller said. slots are empty when the caller hangs up mid-prompt. handle that. dtmf and speech can both fill a slot. test both. a fallback intent should reach a person or a callback. building the bot in lex and forgetting to associate the alias with the instance.

hits.label: Slots become attributes or they vanish
hits.text: slots become attributes or they vanish the agent cannot see a slot you did not copy. after lex returns, copy the slot values into contact attributes with names the crm expects. confirm the slot was filled. an empty slot with a successful intent is normal when the question was optional. session attributes can pass context into the next lex turn. they are not a database. validate the account id in lambda. do not trust a spoken string as authorization. barge-in and touchtone buffering change what the caller can interrupt. log the intent and the confidence behavior you actually configured. keep the bot alias stable. pointing production at a draft alias is how friday breaks. reading the slot in the agent whisper from a name that lex never wrote.

hits.label: Fallback is a route, not a failure
hits.text: fallback is a route, not a failure callers who say something unexpected are still customers. point the fallback intent at a short prompt and a queue, or at a callback when the queue is long. looping the same question more than twice trains people to hang up. use check queue status or get metrics if you want the fallback to behave differently when nobody is staffed. timeout and error are different from fallback. connect them separately. a dtmf escape key should exist even in a speech bot. test with noise, with silence, and with an accent the bot has not heard. do not send fallback into another bot with no exit. a fallback intent that plays 'i didn't get that' forever.

hits.label: Wisdom, Q, and agent assist are one lineage
hits.text: wisdom, q, and agent assist are one lineage using the old name in a design review is fine. using it as the only name in a 2026 runbook is not. wisdom entered preview on 1 december 2020 and became generally available on 27 september 2021. on 28 november 2023 amazon q in connect included that functionality and added generative answers. on 4 august 2026 the admin guide renamed amazon q in connect to agent assist. the service authorization reference still showed the wisdom prefix in september 2026. policies and cli commands can say wisdom or qconnect. read the reference before you write a new policy. connect assistant associates an ai agents domain with the contact. self-service with the assistant was announced 1 december 2024. agentic self-service, including nova sonic for voice, was announced 30 november 2025. agentic cx designer was previewed 22 june 2026 and generally available 2 september 2026. writing a policy for a service name that the iam reference does not use.

hits.label: Turn on assist only where you can show the source
hits.text: turn on assist only where you can show the source a generated sentence without a cited article is not knowledge. it is a guess in the agent's ear. you create a domain, a knowledge base, and content. defaults are 5 assistants, 10 knowledge bases, and 5,000 content items. the connect assistant block attaches the domain to the contact. the agent sees recommendations in the workspace. if the content is wrong, the recommendation is wrong. put an owner and a review date on each article. quick responses and message templates have their own quotas. real-time recommendations need the analytics path enabled for that contact. do not paste customer secrets into a knowledge article. test with a question the article answers and a question it does not. the second test matters more. enabling generative answers on an empty or stale knowledge base.

hits.label: Agentic CX is a flow exit, not a magic queue
hits.text: agentic cx is a flow exit, not a magic queue the application returns an exit condition. your flow must have a branch for each one, including failure. the agentic cx block passes context variables in and routes on the exit condition that comes back. live sync, the new name for voice+, can guide a customer inside a web or mobile app. it is 0.01 usd per minute on top of the channel rate, generally available 2 september 2026, and not billed during the trial through 30 november 2026. external tool calls a tool behind an amazon bedrock agentcore gateway. that is a different block, with a different permission story. map every exit to a queue, a message, or a failure prompt. pass only the attributes the bot needs. keep a dtmf path to a person. load-test the tool. the flow timeout still exists. a single exit arrow labeled 'done' and no error port.

hits.label: Voice ID has ended
hits.text: voice id has ended on 14 october 2026 this feature is already past its end of support. leave the blocks out. new customers stopped on 20 may 2025. support ended on 20 may 2026. after that date the console, the admin site, the ccp, and the voice id resources are not available. the admin guide points at marketplace partners and at a one-time password through aws end user messaging sms. the blocks check voice id and set voice id still appear in the historical block list. adding them to a new flow is a defect. do not grant voiceid iam permissions for a new design. if you still have a domain from before the end date, follow the guide's export and delete steps. do not assume the data remains. authentication for a new design is cognito plus profiles, or your own lambda check. say 'ended' in the migration map so nobody plans a phase around it. scheduling a 2026 phase called 'turn on voice id'.

hits.label: The response contract
hits.text: the response contract connect does not debug your function. it branches. match the block's response validation. a string map is a flat object of strings. json validation allows nested json. the re:post guidance says to keep the payload small, with 32 kb as the figure people hit, and to restrict values to characters connect accepts when you are on a string map. print the contactid. correlate by time only if you forgot. idempotent writes. retries happen. timeouts in the lambda console must be higher than the block timeout or you will add a second failure mode. cold starts count against the 8 seconds. secrets stay in the function environment or in secrets manager, not in flow attributes. returning a python dict with numbers and lists to a string-map block.

hits.label: When the work is slower than eight seconds
hits.text: when the work is slower than eight seconds silence is a defect. async plus a prompt is the pattern. set the block to asynchronous. play a prompt. use wait if you must observe completion, up to 60 seconds. do not chain synchronous calls until you pass 20 seconds in total. if the result is only needed by the agent, write it to a profile or a case and let the workspace load it. the caller does not have to wait on the phone. tell the caller what is happening. a timeout branch still needs a prompt. long work belongs in a queue or a task, not in the greet flow. measure duration in cloudwatch before you argue about the flow. a synchronous chain of four crm calls at the start of every inbound call.

hits.label: Association, resource policy, and the log that says AccessDenied
hits.text: association, resource policy, and the log that says accessdenied the flow log is telling the truth. the function never ran. accessdenied in the flow log means connect could not invoke the function. add the function on the instance and allow connect.amazonaws.com to invoke that version or alias. a permission on the flow author is irrelevant at runtime. if there is no lambda log line at all, you are in this case or the payload was rejected. if there is a log line, the bug is inside the function. use an alias, not $latest, in production. resource-based policy and identity policy answer different questions. vpc-attached functions need a path to their dependency and still must return in time. terraform's association resource is the reviewable form of the console click. adding lambda:invokefunction to the admin user and retesting the call.

hits.label: Queues wait. Profiles decide who is eligible.
hits.text: queues wait. profiles decide who is eligible. a queue with nobody whose profile includes it is a silent parking lot. you create a queue, attach hours, an outbound caller id, and optional quick connects. set working queue selects it. transfer to queue places the contact. the default is 100 queues and 50 queue-channel combinations per routing profile. agent queues are for transfers to a person. the default cap is 10 contacts waiting on one agent queue. priority is per profile, not a property of the queue alone. a contact can sit in a queue that is outside the hours if you never checked hours. callbacks still occupy the queue's logic. they need a staffed profile. name queues for the work, not for a person. building a queue per agent.

hits.label: Priority, delay, and concurrency

hits.text: native forecasting and scheduling native wfm is in the product. third-party wfm is justified when you already live in that suite, not because connect 'cannot schedule'. forecasting predicts volume and handle time and refreshes intraday every 15 minutes. capacity planning turns that into people, using service level and shrinkage. scheduling publishes shifts from skills, patterns, and rules. adherence metrics exist after you publish. the 4 august 2026 rename is forecasting and agent scheduling. agents see shifts in the workspace. time-off rules are not hours of operation. you need history before the forecast is trustworthy. shrinkage is an input you own. the tool does not know your meetings. published schedules are what adherence compares against. a queue with no staffable profile makes the forecast look 'wrong'. buying a second wfm and also turning on native scheduling for the same team.

hits.label: Third-party WFM configuration and faults
hits.text: third-party wfm configuration and faults the integration is the agent event stream plus a historical extract. if either is late, adherence is fiction. aspect's deployment uses one agent-event stream, optionally firehose into s3, and scheduled report exports. eleveo describes the same pair: agent events for the live listener, ctrs and recordings for history. both need a status map. faults: one shard and two consumers, a status renamed in connect and not in the wfm tool, a missed logout, and a schedule that was never published so adherence is blank. give each consumer its own iterator. alarm on iterator age. map statuses in a reviewed table. do not send production events into a vendor lab account. a vpn from the wfm server into the ccp as the 'integration'.

hits.label: Recording and screen capture
hits.text: recording and screen capture if the object is not in s3, you do not have a recording, no matter what the flow block said. set the recording and analytics block on the contact, including outbound whisper flows if outbound must be recorded. the service role writes the wav. the ctr carries the location. screen recording is a separate decision and, on the basic list, 0.006 usd per minute. tell people they are recorded if the law you operate under says so. the prompt is a block, not a policy pdf. customer and agent channels should be identifiable for qm. kms failures look like missing files. a transfer to the pstn ends connect's recording of the far leg. retention is a lifecycle rule you write down. recording only the inbound flow and wondering why outbound disputes have no audio.

hits.label: Third-party recorders and live media
hits.text: third-party recorders and live media some qm suites want the audio while the call is up. that is kinesis video streams, not a second sip trunk. start media streaming opens live customer audio. stop media streaming ends it. third-party tools consume the stream. a tool in another account needs the stream arn from the contact event and an iam role that can read it. after the call, many tools also import the wav from s3 using the ctr. faults: streaming never started because the block was skipped, the cross-account role is wrong, or the tool looks for a stereo file connect did not write in the shape it expects. read the tool's format note. do not guess pcm layout. streaming and s3 recording can both be on. know which one the evaluator uses. stop the stream. leaked streams cost money and keep audio you meant to end. do not stream calls that your policy says must not be recorded. test cross-account access with a security review, not with a long-lived access key. mirroring the rtp to a recorder vm on a shelf.

hits.label: Quality management on top of analytics
hits.text: quality management on top of analytics a score without the recording is an opinion. a recording without a form is an archive. evaluation forms were previewed 29 november 2022 and became generally available 26 april 2023. they sit with conversational analytics. you can score a contact, calibrate reviewers, and coach. generative scoring, where you turn it on, is still a score someone must be willing to defend. the quota table limits how many evaluation questions ai may answer on one contact. read that limit before you design a 40-question form and assume a model fills it. calibrate reviewers on the same five contacts. the transcript can miss a word. the audio decides. redaction must run before a reviewer who should not see the secret sees the form. coaching is a workflow. the form is not the coaching. auto-failing an agent on a summary that paraphrased badly.

hits.label: Configure conversational analytics and fix the empty transcript
hits.text: configure conversational analytics and fix the empty transcript analytics that is not enabled on the contact produces an empty search and a false 'the feature is down'. enable the analytics behavior on the recording block for the flows that need it, including the outbound whisper if outbound matters. confirm the language. confirm redaction. check the real-time quota if supervisors say rules never fire during a storm. post-call jobs scale with minutes. use the quota page's 40 percent rule of thumb to see if you are out of job concurrency. names: the console may say conversational analytics. your old diagram may say contact lens. search both. a flow that sets recording off 'for this queue' also kills the transcript. rules on keywords need the real-time path. summaries are absent until the post-contact job finishes. chat analytics is a separate enablement from voice. it arrived later and is configured on the chat contact. opening a support case for 'contact lens missing' on a flow that never set the block.

hits.label: E911 for agents on the CCP
hits.text: e911 for agents on the ccp a contact-center platform is not automatically an emergency-calling design. in the us regions where this exists, you still have to store a real address. direct 911 from the ccp is enabled by default in us east (n. virginia), us west (oregon), and govcloud us-west. connect does not transfer a live call to 911 and does not let an agent dial 911 while already on a call. e911 sends a validated physical address. you validate with the chime validatee911address api, store it on the agent's customer profile, and an outbound whisper flow copies it to the civicaddress attribute when the dialed string is 911. test with 933. it reads back the number and the address. the docs describe a 100 usd penalty for a non-emergency 911 call. the origination number must be callable if responders need to ring back. create a task in that whisper flow so security is notified. home agents must update the address when they move. a cucm elin for the office does not cover them. civicaddress is a json string, not a json object. the keys include country, a1, a3, hno, rd, sts, and pc. prompt agents to confirm the address at the start of a shift if they roam. this is not available as a transfer from a customer call. outside those regions, do not invent a 911 design. use the local emergency method and say so. telling home agents to dial 911 on the ccp while the stored address is the headquarters.

hits.label: CRM configuration and the faults that look like routing bugs
hits.text: crm configuration and the faults that look like routing bugs a wrong screen pop is often an attribute bug, not a salesforce bug. salesforce: sandbox, package, ccp embed or scc-ac, one case owner, click-to-dial. servicenow: imported flows, queue map, hold file under 5 seconds, one router. both need the customer id written before the agent is offered the contact. faults: pop on the wrong record because ani matched a household, a blank pop because the attribute name does not match the softphone layout, a double agent because awa and connect both routed, and a transfer to cucm that strands the crm because the second leg has no contactid. log the attribute in the flow and in the crm activity. search profiles before creating a lead. outbound click-to-dial uses the queue caller id. retest after every managed-package upgrade in a sandbox. opening the crm with a hard-coded account so the demo works.

hits.label: AI agents: configure, cite, and a way out
hits.text: ai agents: configure, cite, and a way out an agent who cannot reach a person is not assisted. they are stuck. attach the domain with the connect assistant block only on flows where the knowledge base has an owner. for self-service, the agentic cx exit conditions must include failure and 'human'. external tool calls need a permission review. live sync is optional and priced. faults: empty recommendations because the block never ran, answers from a stale article, a policy written for the wrong iam prefix, and a bot that consumes the 8-second lambda budget inside a tool call. every generated answer in a design review needs the article title. keep dtmf escape. do not send payment card data into a prompt. voice id is not the fallback. it has ended. turning on generative self-service for the main number on day one.

hits.label: Integration maps
hits.text: integration maps a map is a list of seams with a key on each line. a poster of logos is not a map. seam examples this campus will draw in the lab: salesforce embed, servicenow queue map, teams chat, cucm transfer, wfm agent events, qm via s3 or kvs, e911 whisper, analytics stream. each row has a producer, a consumer, a key, a protocol, and the first fault to check. if you cannot name the key, you are not ready to build the seam. contactid joins contact-scoped tools. profile id joins customer-scoped tools. agent arn or username joins wfm. civicaddress joins only the 911 whisper. an arrow labeled 'integrates'.

hits.label: Future hooks, not future rewrites
hits.text: future hooks, not future rewrites add the next system on a hook that already exists. do not scrape the ccp and do not fork the flow for every vendor. hooks you can adopt later: eventbridge contact events, the ctr stream, agent events, kinesis video, customer profiles events, cases, show view, data tables, external tool, and the flow language json in your pipeline. live sync and agentic cx are the 2026 hooks for guided and agentic experiences. a hook has a schema and a permission. write both down when you 'leave room' for a vendor. room without a schema is a hope. prefer events over polling the real-time api. prefer attributes over asking the agent to retype. prefer a module for a policy that every future flow must share. re-read the quota before you promise a vendor a fan-out. a custom browser extension that clicks the ccp.

hits.label: Contact
hits.text: contact one interaction: a call, chat, task, or email. a transfer usually creates another contact linked by previouscontactid and nextcontactid.

hits.label: Instance
hits.text: instance the connect container in one region. it holds users, flows, queues, and numbers. a new account starts at two instances per region.

hits.label: Contact flow
hits.text: contact flow the visual program a contact runs. the json form is the flow language.

hits.label: Flow module
hits.text: flow module a published, reusable piece of a flow. invoke module runs it. return ends it. default quota is 200 modules.

hits.label: Contact attribute
hits.text: contact attribute a string key and value stored on the contact. lambda, lex, and set contact attributes write them. screen pop reads them.

hits.label: Customer queue flow
hits.text: customer queue flow the interruptible flow that runs while the customer waits, before an agent joins.

hits.label: Whisper flow
hits.text: whisper flow audio played to one party immediately before the customer and agent are joined.

hits.label: Working queue
hits.text: working queue the queue selected by set working queue. transfer to queue uses it.

hits.label: Routing profile
hits.text: routing profile the list of queues an agent can receive, with channel concurrency, priority, and delay.

hits.label: Priority
hits.text: priority a number on a queue inside a routing profile. a lower number is served first.

hits.label: Delay
hits.text: delay seconds a contact must wait before an agent with that profile can receive it.

hits.label: Routing criteria
hits.text: routing criteria ordered steps that tighten or relax who can take the contact. the successor idea to precision-queue steps.

hits.label: Proficiency
hits.text: proficiency a level on a predefined attribute for an agent. default quota is 10 proficiencies per agent.

hits.label: Queue
hits.text: queue where a contact waits. standard queues hold customers. agent queues hold transfers to a specific user, 10 contacts each by default.

hits.label: Hours of operation
hits.text: hours of operation the weekly schedule and time zone attached to a queue. check hours of operation reads it. overrides cover holidays.

hits.label: Quick connect
hits.text: quick connect a one-click transfer target: a user, a queue, or an external number.

hits.label: DID
hits.text: did a direct inward dial number. in the us it is carried by one carrier and priced per day plus per minute.

hits.label: Toll-free number
hits.text: toll-free number a number the caller does not pay long-distance to dial. us toll-free numbers are registered with somos and can use more than one carrier.

hits.label: UIFN
hits.text: uifn universal international freephone number. one of the four number types connect sells, with did, toll-free, and shared cost.

hits.label: Porting
hits.text: porting moving a number from another carrier onto connect. the quota page points you at the same support form used for quota increases.

hits.label: CCP
hits.text: ccp contact control panel. the browser phone and contact ui the agent uses.

hits.label: Agent workspace
hits.text: agent workspace the fuller desktop around the ccp: profiles, cases, step-by-step views, and third-party apps.

hits.label: Streams API
hits.text: streams api the amazon-connect-streams library. it embeds or replaces the ccp and listens to agent and contact events.

hits.label: Softphone media
hits.text: softphone media the webrtc audio path. it needs outbound udp 3478 to the regional turnnlb domain.

hits.label: TURN
hits.text: turn the relay used when the browser cannot send media directly. the error text names turn:turnnlb-....elb.region.amazonaws.com:3478.

hits.label: Lex V2
hits.text: lex v2 the bot service get customer input calls. connect stores intent and slots on the contact.

hits.label: Intent
hits.text: intent what lex thinks the caller wants. the flow branches on it.

hits.label: Slot
hits.text: slot a value lex fills, such as an order id. the flow copies it into an attribute.

hits.label: Agent assist
hits.text: agent assist the 4 aug 2026 name for the feature previously called amazon q in connect, which itself included wisdom.

hits.label: Amazon Q in Connect
hits.text: amazon q in connect the 2023 name for generative assistance. the admin guide renamed it agent assist on 4 aug 2026. iam still shows the wisdom prefix.

hits.label: Wisdom
hits.text: wisdom the 2020 preview name for agent search and recommendations. folded into amazon q in connect on 28 nov 2023.

hits.label: Connect assistant block
hits.text: connect assistant block associates an ai agents domain with the contact so recommendations can run.

hits.label: Agentic CX
hits.text: agentic cx a block that hands the contact to an agentic cx designer application and routes on the exit condition.

hits.label: Live Sync
hits.text: live sync the 4 aug 2026 name for voice+. priced at 0.01 usd per minute on top of the channel. trial through 30 nov 2026 is not billed.

hits.label: Conversational analytics
hits.text: conversational analytics the 4 aug 2026 name for contact lens: transcripts, sentiment, redaction, summaries, and categories.

hits.label: Contact Lens
hits.text: contact lens the former name of conversational analytics. the product page says the function remains.

hits.label: Real-time analytics
hits.text: real-time analytics rules on a live contact, announced 1 dec 2020. default quota is 300 concurrent real-time analytics calls.

hits.label: Post-contact summary
hits.text: post-contact summary a generated summary after the contact. preview 28 nov 2023, generally available 25 mar 2024.

hits.label: Evaluation form
hits.text: evaluation form a quality scorecard. preview 29 nov 2022, generally available 26 apr 2023. now part of performance evaluations.

hits.label: CTR
hits.text: ctr contact trace record. the json document for a finished contact, streamed to kinesis or firehose.

hits.label: Agent event stream
hits.text: agent event stream near real-time kinesis stream of login, logout, status, and contact join. this is the wfm adherence feed.

hits.label: Flow log
hits.text: flow log a cloudwatch log of each block. set logging behavior turns it on. the log group is under the instance.

hits.label: Lambda synchronous timeout
hits.text: lambda synchronous timeout at most 8 seconds. the function's own timeout can be longer. the flow still takes the error or timeout branch at 8 seconds.

hits.label: Lambda asynchronous mode
hits.text: lambda asynchronous mode the flow continues without waiting. you can wait up to 60 seconds with a wait block. a sequence of lambda calls must finish within 20 seconds.

hits.label: String map
hits.text: string map a flat object of string keys and string values. one of the two lambda response shapes.

hits.label: Customer Profiles
hits.text: customer profiles the profile store. connect-generated profiles are priced differently from profiles that contain imported data.

hits.label: Identity resolution
hits.text: identity resolution the rules that merge profile records from crm, orders, and contacts into one customer.

hits.label: Case
hits.text: case a durable issue that can span many contacts. cases became generally available on 3 oct 2022.

hits.label: Task
hits.text: task a unit of work with no live media. default concurrent quota is 2500. tasks can be scheduled up to 90 days ahead.

hits.label: Security profile
hits.text: security profile what a user may do in the admin site and the ccp. different from an iam policy.

hits.label: IAM policy
hits.text: iam policy what an aws principal may call. connect, profiles, cases, and agent assist use different iam prefixes.

hits.label: Service-linked role
hits.text: service-linked role the role aws creates so connect can write to s3, cloudwatch, and other services you name.

hits.label: KMS key policy
hits.text: kms key policy the key's own allow list. recordings stay unreadable if the key does not trust the connect role.

hits.label: SAML
hits.text: saml the federated sign-in option. the assertion must carry the routing profile, security profile, and role.

hits.label: IAM Identity Center
hits.text: iam identity center a common identity provider in front of connect. it still speaks saml to the instance.

hits.label: Global Resiliency
hits.text: global resiliency the supported multi-region design. pairs are us-east-1 with us-west-2, eu-central-1 with eu-west-2, and ap-northeast-1 with ap-northeast-3.

hits.label: Traffic distribution group
hits.text: traffic distribution group the object that splits telephony and agent sign-in across the two regions in 10 percent steps.

hits.label: Replica instance
hits.text: replica instance the linked instance created by replicateinstance. flows, users, queues, and profiles are copied. s3 prompts are not.

hits.label: Connect Customer
hits.text: connect customer the name used from 28 apr 2026 for the contact center product previously called amazon connect.

hits.label: Connect Customer Basic
hits.text: connect customer basic the form of the product that does not include every connect customer feature. voice on this form is listed at 0.018 usd per minute plus telephony.

hits.label: Voice ID
hits.text: voice id caller authentication and a fraudster watchlist. new customers stopped 20 may 2025. support ended 20 may 2026.

hits.label: Outbound campaign
hits.text: outbound campaign proactive voice, sms, or email. the name replaced high-volume outbound communications on 20 jun 2022. voice minutes are 0.045 usd on connect customer.

hits.label: Check call progress
hits.text: check call progress the block that branches on answering-machine detection. campaign flows only.

hits.label: Persistent chat
hits.text: persistent chat a chat that can go quiet without holding a concurrent-chat slot the way an abandoned idle chat does.

hits.label: WhatsApp
hits.text: whatsapp a third-party messaging channel counted inside the concurrent chat quota. connect customer prices the message at 0.014 usd before delivery fees.

hits.label: Email thread
hits.text: email thread replies within 90 days stay on the same thread. later replies start a new one.

hits.label: Data table
hits.text: data table rows the data table block can read or write inside a flow. defaults: 100 tables, 5 primary attributes, 1000 values.

hits.label: Show view
hits.text: show view renders a step-by-step view in the agent workspace.

hits.label: External Tool
hits.text: external tool invokes a tool through an amazon bedrock agentcore gateway.

hits.label: Start media streaming
hits.text: start media streaming sends live customer audio to kinesis video streams for a third-party recorder or bot.

hits.label: Screen recording
hits.text: screen recording records the agent desktop. on the basic price list it is 0.006 usd per minute.

hits.label: Forecasting and agent scheduling
hits.text: forecasting and agent scheduling the 4 aug 2026 name for native wfm: forecast, capacity, schedules, and adherence.

hits.label: Schedule adherence
hits.text: schedule adherence how closely an agent's actual status matched the published schedule. native metrics appear after schedules are published. third-party wfm reads agent events.

hits.label: Shrinkage
hits.text: shrinkage the fraction of paid time that is not handling contacts. erlang staffing divides raw agents by one minus shrinkage.

hits.label: Service level
hits.text: service level the share of contacts answered inside a target wait. queue.duration on the ctr is the usual clock.

hits.label: Occupancy
hits.text: occupancy handle time plus acw, divided by signed-in time that was available for work. agent events supply the clocks.

hits.label: ACW
hits.text: acw after contact work. the agent is still busy after the customer leaves. it counts in occupancy and in the concurrent task and email quotas.

hits.label: E911
hits.text: e911 us enhanced 911. for a us agent, connect can send a validated civic address with a direct 911 call from the ccp.
933 the test number that reads back the originating number and the address. use it instead of a real 911 test. a non-emergency 911 call is described as a 100 usd penalty.

hits.label: CivicAddress
hits.text: civicaddress the contact attribute that carries the e911 address as a json string. keys include country, a1, a3, hno, rd, sts, and pc.

hits.label: ValidateE911Address
hits.text: validatee911address the amazon chime api that checks an address against the master street address guide before you store it.

hits.label: Salesforce CTI Adapter
hits.text: salesforce cti adapter a managed package plus a serverless app that embeds the ccp in salesforce.

hits.label: SCC-AC
hits.text: scc-ac salesforce contact center with amazon connect. voice stays on connect. messaging can be connect or salesforce.

hits.label: ServiceNow Voice
hits.text: servicenow voice the servicenow integration that imports flows, maps queues to advanced work assignment, and can attach ai voice agents.

hits.label: Teams chat bridge
hits.text: teams chat bridge a published pattern: a teams app, azure bot service, api gateway, lambda, and startchatcontact. it is chat, not a phone trunk.

hits.label: External voice connector
hits.text: external voice connector analytics on audio that stays on another platform. the appendix lists 0.032 usd per minute and 100 usd per connector per day.

hits.label: CloudWatch
hits.text: cloudwatch metrics and flow logs. alarm at 80 percent of a quota, which is the operations guidance in the email quota note.

hits.label: Kinesis Data Streams
hits.text: kinesis data streams the durable stream for ctrs and agent events when more than one consumer must read them.

hits.label: Kinesis Data Firehose
hits.text: kinesis data firehose the delivery path into s3. it buffers. silence for five minutes is the point to check the error prefix.

hits.label: Kinesis Video Streams
hits.text: kinesis video streams live audio for third-party recorders. start media streaming opens it. customer and agent audio are separate tracks.

hits.label: EventBridge
hits.text: eventbridge the bus for contact events if you want a rule, not a stream consumer.

hits.label: S3 recording object
hits.text: s3 recording object the wav connect writes when recording is on. third-party qm tools often import this object plus the ctr.

hits.label: Erlang
hits.text: erlang the unit of traffic. one erlang is one hour of call time in one hour. calls per hour times aht in hours.

hits.label: Erlang C
hits.text: erlang c the probability a contact waits when there are n agents and a erlangs, assuming infinite queue and random arrivals.

hits.label: AHT
hits.text: aht average handle time. talk plus hold plus acw, unless your report defines it more narrowly. say which one you used.

hits.label: Region pair
hits.text: region pair the only regions global resiliency links. osaka is a replica region for tokyo, and inbound delivery there can take up to 20 seconds.

hits.label: Option 1 network allow list
hits.text: option 1 network allow list domains instead of the whole ec2 and cloudfront ip ranges. recommended. test more than 200 calls. an error rate above 2 percent means the proxy may be the problem.

hits.label: Stateless firewall
hits.text: stateless firewall must allow the browser's ephemeral udp range back in, or media fails even when 3478 is allowed outbound.

hits.label: my.connect.aws
hits.text: my.connect.aws the current instance domain. awsapps.com is the old domain the docs say is going away.

hits.label: Concurrent calls quota
hits.text: concurrent calls quota default 10 active pstn and webrtc calls. this is the first capacity gate on a new instance.

hits.label: Quota lead time
hits.text: quota lead time small raises can be hours. large ones can take up to three weeks. a worldwide raise can take months.

hits.label: Cloud Practitioner
hits.text: cloud practitioner the foundational aws certification. it covers the shared vocabulary of accounts, regions, and billing. it is not a connect exam.

hits.label: Solutions Architect - Associate
hits.text: solutions architect - associate the associate exam that best matches the aws services a connect design uses.

hits.label: Communications Specialist badge
hits.text: communications specialist badge a skill builder and credly badge. pass mark is 80 percent. it is not an aws certification exam.

hits.label: Advanced Networking - Specialty
hits.text: advanced networking - specialty the networking specialty exam. last day to take it is 31 december 2026.

hits.label: Calling search space
hits.text: calling search space cucm's list of partitions a phone may dial. the connect cousin is a routing profile, and they do not configure each other.

hits.label: CSQ
hits.text: csq a uccx contact service queue. map it to a connect queue, not to a routing profile.

hits.label: Precision queue
hits.text: precision queue a ucce queue with attribute steps. map the steps to routing criteria, not to one flat skill group.

hits.label: Finesse
hits.text: finesse the cisco agent desktop. the connect cousins are the ccp, the agent workspace, and a streams application.

hits.label: CUIC
hits.text: cuic cisco unified intelligence center. the connect cousins are real-time metrics, historical metrics, and the ctr.

hits.label: VDN
hits.text: vdn an avaya vector directory number. map it to a phone number plus the flow that number starts.

hits.label: Partition
hits.text: partition cucm's dial-plan bucket. connect has no partitions. numbers are claimed, ported, or reached with transfer to phone number.

hits.label: Shared responsibility
hits.text: shared responsibility aws runs the region, the softphone service, and the multi-tenant platform. you run flows, iam, keys, numbers, quotas, and the agent network.

hits.label: Flow language action
hits.text: flow language action one json step. types are contact, participant, interaction, or flow control.

hits.label: Error branch
hits.text: error branch the path a block takes when it fails. an unconnected error branch ends the contact.

hits.label: Screen pop
hits.text: screen pop opening the customer record when the contact arrives. connect does this with attributes, profiles, and a workspace app. it is not a cti cable.

hits.label: AppIntegrations
hits.text: appintegrations the account-level service that attaches data and event integrations. default is 20 data integrations per region.

hits.label: Hook
hits.text: hook a supported place to attach the next system: a stream, an event, a block, or a workspace view. build on a hook instead of scraping the ccp.

hits.label: Mind map
hits.text: mind map the one-page picture of which system owns telephony, the agent, the record, the score, and the emergency call.

hits.label: Quality management
hits.text: quality management scoring contacts against a form, coaching from the score, and keeping the recording that proves it.

hits.label: Redaction
hits.text: redaction removing sensitive data from a transcript or recording. conversational analytics can redact. confirm the rule before you promise a regulator it is on.

hits.label: Category
hits.text: category a rules match on words, sentiment, or silence. supervisors subscribe to categories. they are not intents.

hits.label: Intraday forecast
hits.text: intraday forecast a rest-of-day volume prediction. native forecasting updates it every 15 minutes.

hits.label: Capacity plan
hits.text: capacity plan how many agents you need for a service level, a handle time, and a shrinkage assumption.

hits.label: Time-off rule
hits.text: time-off rule the constraint native scheduling uses when an agent requests leave. it is not the same object as hours of operation.

hits.label: Origination number
hits.text: origination number the caller id sent with an outbound or 911 call. responders can call it back only if that number accepts inbound calls.

hits.label: Master Street Address Guide
hits.text: master street address guide the address database validatee911address checks. a free-typed address is not enough.

hits.label: On-site notification
hits.text: on-site notification the task the 911 whisper flow creates so security or hr knows a 911 call was placed.

hits.label: Dual-run
hits.text: dual-run keeping the old platform and connect both able to receive the number while you compare flows, reports, and failover.

hits.label: Rollback
hits.text: rollback the tested path back to the old platform or the other region. a port without a rollback date is not a plan.

hits.label: Get metrics block
hits.text: get metrics block reads real-time queue and agent metrics into attributes so a flow can branch on them.

hits.label: Interrupt agent
hits.text: interrupt agent offers a contact to a named agent even if that agent is at maximum concurrency or in a custom status.

hits.label: Touchtone buffer
hits.text: touchtone buffer lets the caller type ahead. set touchtone buffer behavior controls it.

hits.label: Distribute by percentage
hits.text: distribute by percentage sends a share of contacts down each branch. use it for a measured pilot, not for skills.

hits.label: Analytics data lake
hits.text: analytics data lake zero-etl contact data that athena or quicksight can query. previewed 28 nov 2023.

hits.label: GetMetricDataV2
hits.text: getmetricdatav2 the metrics api you want for new dashboards. it is the current metrics call, as opposed to the older getmetricdata.

hits.text: name the seam. salesforce and servicenow screen-pop on contactid and the attributes you copied. teams is a different client. a pbx beside connect is a telephony seam. the crm record should store contactid. without it the recording and the case never meet. lambda that writes to the crm still has eight seconds if the flow is waiting on it. pop the screen from attributes you already have, and let the slow write finish off the voice path. a pbx kept beside connect needs one dial plan. two systems claiming the same did will split the calls. a screen pop that keys on the caller's raw ani will open the wrong record for every shared main number. cti and the contact flow are not the same integration. one watches agent state. the other decides the caller path. microsoft teams as a phone and the ccp as a phone, both for the same agent, fight over the headset and the state. an integration that only works in the demo org, with a hard-coded account id, is the example arn problem. replace it before you publish. screen pop contactid plus the attribute you matched, such as the account slot. cti agent state and the contact event. often the agent-event stream. lambda seam only if the flow can survive eight seconds, or the call is async. salesforce / servicenow the case or incident stores contactid. teams a client. not the contact flow. pbx one owner of the did. the other system gets an overflow or a tie line, on purpose.

hits.label: Ecosystem cheat sheet
hits.text: workforce management wants agent events and adherence against a published shift. connect forecasting is not a third-party wfm product, and a third-party product is not the native forecast. recording and quality can be native or external. either way the recording has to join on contactid. for us ccp agents, store the address they are actually at and test with 933. a headquarters address on a home agent is a wrong dispatch. 933 is the test number in this campus. it is not a live 911 call, and a lab result is not an emergency-calling certification. assuming the office e911 design covers an agent on the ccp at home. a wfm schedule that never reads after-contact work will mark a careful agent as out of adherence. quality forms that score sentiment and ignore the redaction rule will coach people on a card number that should not have been stored. future hooks are configuration and events, not a fork of the contact flow for every new vendor. wfm agent events in. adherence compares the shift with the state, including acw. forecast native forecasting and agent scheduling, or a third-party tool. name which. recording s3 via the instance, or an external recorder. join on contactid. e911 per-agent address. test with 933. not the hq default. quality form plus categories. redaction before the transcript is retained. hook event, attribute, or an existing block. not a second copy of the flow.
